heroSection.headline: Omada Switches
heroSection.subtext: A complete range of enterprise-grade network switches providing high-performance, scalable, and centrally managed solutions for any business need. From the core to the edge, Omada has you covered.

technologyHighlights.title: Centralized Cloud Management with Omada SDN
technologyHighlights.description: The Omada Software Defined Networking (SDN) platform integrates network devices, including switches, access points and gateways, providing 100% centralized cloud management. Create a highly scalable network—all controlled from a single interface. Seamless wireless and wired connections are provided, ideal for use in hospitality, education, retail, offices, and more.

technologyHighlights.title: Advanced Power over Ethernet (PoE)
technologyHighlights.description: Simplify your deployments with Power over Ethernet. Omada switches support various PoE standards, including PoE+ (802.3at) and PoE++ (802.3bt), with budgets up to 1440W. Power devices like IP cameras, VoIP phones, and access points directly over the Ethernet cable, without the need for separate power adapters. Features like PoE Auto Recovery and Extended PoE Range add reliability and flexibility.

technologyHighlights.title: High-Speed Networking
technologyHighlights.description: Eliminate bottlenecks with a range of high-speed port options. Omada switches offer everything from Gigabit Ethernet to 2.5G Multi-Gigabit, 10G, and even 25G fiber ports, ensuring your network can handle high-bandwidth tasks and future growth with ease.

faqs.question: What is the benefit of a managed switch over an unmanaged one?
faqs.answer: Managed switches, like most Omada models, offer greater control over your network. You can configure features like VLANs for security, QoS to prioritize traffic, and monitor network health. Unmanaged switches are simple plug-and-play devices for basic network expansion with no configuration options.

faqs.question: Do I need an Omada Controller to use Omada managed switches?
faqs.answer: While not required (switches can be managed in standalone mode via a web interface or CLI), using an Omada SDN Controller (hardware, software, or cloud-based) unlocks centralized management, allowing you to control your entire network of switches, access points, and gateways from a single dashboard.

faqs.question: Can I connect a non-PoE device to a PoE port?
faqs.answer: Yes. PoE ports are smart and will only supply power if they detect a PoE-compatible device. If you plug in a non-PoE device like a laptop or printer, the port will function as a standard data-only Ethernet port without any risk of damage.

faqs.question: What is the difference between PoE, PoE+, and PoE++?
faqs.answer: These standards define the maximum power that can be delivered over an Ethernet cable. PoE (802.3af) delivers up to 15.4W. PoE+ (802.3at) delivers up to 30W, suitable for devices like VoIP phones and dual-band APs. PoE++ (802.3bt) is the latest standard, delivering 60W (Type 3) or 90-100W (Type 4), required for high-power devices like pan-tilt-zoom cameras and Wi-Fi 6/7 access points.
